Neither pass left a test, so the pill box, the type ramp and the accent rule have been unguarded since. NOW GUARDED: src/components/streaming/StreamRewardsTicker.figma.test.tsx, 13 tests, reading the pill fill and the two accents as resolved rgb() and every geometry value as a NUMBER parsed out of its utility. Mutation-proved against the pre-2026-09-01 shape (rounded-lg + border + bg-muted, one flat text-xs at font-medium, px-4 py-4 on the strip): 6 of 13 red. AND A STALE CLAIM IN streamRewards.ts IS CORRECTED - not in the component but in the module its data comes from. Both its module docblock and its is_highlighted field doc still described Frame 718 as an outlined pill. status.wave9.social-live.tsv:12 records the opposite off 11529-293404: same #001615 fill, no stroke, and what differs is that with no amount to carry the accent the HANDLE takes it instead of #95A09F. The docblocks now state that rule, and say plainly that keying it off is_highlighted is a choice the artwork permits rather than one it proves. CARRIED FORWARD FROM status.wave11.social-live.tsv:12-14, credited and not re-derived, because this row supersedes it: SHELL Frame 429 bare; Frame 299 pad4/16/0/16 fill #122524 with a bottom-only #123F3C w1 hairline; Frame 300 pad16 with the top hairline and DROP_SHADOW blur80 offset 0,10 #000000@0.25; both band radii 16 at 1440 and 12 at 768 and 375; Frame 300 itemSpacing 36 except 24 at 375. All of that is what StreamChat.tsx ships and it is unchanged here. STILL partial, AND THE OPEN ITEM IS UNCHANGED: which pill gets which accent. Two donors and two colours (#FFFF16 / #17F9B4) is equally consistent with per-donor tinting and with a highlight flag and the artwork distinguishes neither, so the oracle pins the RULE the frame does settle - one accent per pill, on the amount when there is one and on the handle when there is not, gift glyph always following it - and deliberately does not pin which pill is which. THIS BOARD SETS THE THIRD TYPE STEP AND THE ONLY HEIGHT STEP: Frame 755 is 429x26 with pills at h26 and Mulish Regular 14/18, against h24 and 14/16 at 768 and h24 and 12/14 at 375. The oracle reads the height and the leading as numbers at each step and asserts the 768 step writes NO height of its own, which is what makes the 26 a desktop value rather than a floor.
